text:
Marathon Petroleum bounced back 1.6% today after three straight days of losses that wiped out 10% of the stock's value last week. The recovery reflects modest stabilization in crude oil markets — US oil held steady around $100/barrel, and refineries continue running at a healthy 94.5% capacity. Conflicting signals about Iran tensions may have eased some of the panic: while Trump administration officials expressed optimism about ending the conflict, oil markets also briefly dipped below $90 when that rhetoric circulated, before stabilizing today.

The bigger picture is that refiner stocks are caught between two opposing forces right now. Lower oil prices and high fuel inventories (gasoline stocks are near recent levels) would normally hurt refining margins, but the 10% drop over two weeks suggests investors were pricing in more severe oil price declines tied to geopolitical de-escalation — a decline that didn't fully materialize today, allowing the stock to recover somewhat.
